skill.name: image-inpainting
skill.description: Guides an AI agent through mask-driven image inpainting with the RunComfy CLI. It selects Z-Image Turbo Inpainting for image and mask URLs, suggests fallback edit models without masks, and explains strength and output options.
skill.summary: Run mask-based local image edits through RunComfy.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The static detections are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline code spans, documentation links, and a documented token path. No prompt injection attempt, hidden command execution, or malicious filesystem access was found. A semantic content risk remains because the skill explicitly supports watermark removal without an ownership or authorization guard.

remediation.issue: Watermark removal is presented as a normal workflow without an authorization check.
remediation.suggestion: Remove broad watermark removal triggers and examples, or require explicit confirmation that the user owns the image or has permission.

remediation.issue: Image and mask URLs are processed by an external hosted service.
remediation.suggestion: Keep a clear privacy notice and advise users not to submit private or regulated images unless their policy allows it.

content.value_statement: Local image edits are hard when a region must change without disturbing the rest of the image. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through mask-based RunComfy inpainting with clear model choices and parameters.
actual_capabilities: Routes masked edits to Z-Image Turbo Inpainting through the RunComfy CLI.
Accepts source image URLs, grayscale mask URLs, prompts, strength, and control scale settings.
Guides object removal, region replacement, background swaps, and blemish cleanup workflows.
Suggests description-based edit models when no mask is available.
Explains output directory behavior, exit codes, and troubleshooting paths for RunComfy jobs.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI to be installed and authenticated before execution.
The mask-driven route needs externally reachable source image and mask URLs.
It does not create masks, extend canvases, or edit video frames.
Image content is processed by RunComfy, so use only authorized and policy-approved assets.

use_cases.title: Clean Product Photos
use_cases.description: Remove stray objects or damaged pixels from product photos while keeping packaging edges, shadows, and texture consistent.

use_cases.title: Replace Masked Backgrounds
use_cases.description: Replace a masked backdrop with a clean studio setting and tune strength for the desired amount of change.

use_cases.title: Automate Edit Runs
use_cases.description: Ask an agent to choose the RunComfy model, prepare parameters, and explain expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Remove a Masked Object
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a source image and mask.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use image-inpainting on this source image and mask URL. Remove the selected object, preserve the surrounding texture, and explain the chosen strength.

prompt_templates.title: Swap a Background
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a full masked region replacement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Z-Image Turbo Inpainting to replace only the masked background. Keep the product unchanged and choose strength for a full background swap.

prompt_templates.title: Edit Without a Mask
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request where the region is described in words.
prompt_templates.prompt: I do not have a mask for this edit. Pick the best description-based fallback, remove only the described region, and protect the rest of the image.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Batch Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning before multiple RunComfy executions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an inpainting run for these images and masks. Recommend model, strength, control scale, naming, retries, and review checks before execution.

output_examples.input: A user provides a street photo and a cable mask.
output_examples.output: The agent selects Z-Image Turbo Inpainting, uses low strength, preserves the skyline, and reports where the edited image was saved.

output_examples.input: A designer asks to replace a masked product backdrop.
output_examples.output: The agent recommends high strength, describes a clean studio background, and keeps the product outside the mask unchanged.

output_examples.input: A user has no mask but describes an unwanted corner object.
output_examples.output: The agent chooses a description-based fallback model and warns that mask-free edits may be less precise.

best_practices: Use a grayscale mask with slightly softened edges for cleaner blending.
Describe both the replacement content and the areas that must stay unchanged.
Confirm image rights and third-party processing approval before sending assets to RunComfy.
anti_patterns: Removing watermarks or ownership marks from content without confirmed authorization.
Using rough masks that cover important nearby details and then expecting precise preservation.
Requesting broad scene redesigns without a mask while expecting pixel-exact local edits.

faq.question: Does this skill create masks?
faq.answer: No. It expects image and mask URLs from the user or an upstream masking tool.

faq.question: Can it work without a mask?
faq.answer: Yes. It can route to description-based image edit models, but edges may be less precise.

faq.question: Does it send images outside my environment?
faq.answer: Yes. RunComfy processes the image and mask URLs through its hosted service.

faq.question: Can I use it for private or regulated images?
faq.answer: Only use it when your policy allows third-party processing of the image content.

faq.question: Can it remove watermarks?
faq.answer: Use it only for marks on content you own or are authorized to edit.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
